what: Every declared kernel that NEITHER emitter places. This is the tile-rs acceptance backlog: the point of keeping it is that a kernel the AscendC and PTO paths both refuse should still be a target the lift can take, rather than being dropped from the inventory. `rust/tests/test_tile_rs_acceptance.py` keeps this in step with the manifests, so a kernel that starts placing must leave the file. Each entry also records `needs`: the mechanism that would place it. A backlog without that is a list of complaints. One correction: an earlier version of this file said rspto had no chunked path. It has one for blocked matmul, and since 2026-11-08 one for a LONG DOT -- a `1 x W` load/load/mul/reduce_sum/store chain whose row does not fit the unified buffer, emitted as unrolled chunks whose products are folded before a single reduction. That closed six of the ten entries that named `the chunked path GENERALISED`. Of the four that remained, the 8-row QUANTIZE closed on 2026-11-08 after four repairs -- the chunked path was narrowing and loop-offsetting every operand rather than only the width-sized ones, `alloc_tile_typed` was discarding custom tile types under chunking, a `1 x 1` scale needed the padded 32-byte-floor idiom, and the arm had to broadcast the per-tensor scale (`tcolexpand` down the rows, `trowexpanddiv` along them) instead of dividing by it elementwise, which ptoas refuses on valid_shape. The 8-row RMSNORM closed on 2026-11-08 too, as the two-pass arm that entry asked for: fold the per-chunk squares, one `trowsum` after the fold, then re-read each chunk and scale it by the broadcast inverse. TWO are left and neither is a chunking problem: both argmaxes carry a running INDEX that a chunk boundary restarts, and their input plane cannot be resident at all -- 21.6x and 21.3x the addressable UB -- so no emitter arm reaches them. See the campaign's scripts/residency_check.py. 2026-11-08: gemm_f16_lmhead_v41_16x5120x16160 left this file and CAME BACK the same day, and the round trip is worth keeping. It was removed because its ascendc entry recorded a UB overflow ('buffer 0 needs 81920 elements') that the emitter appeared no longer to hit -- removed correctly by this file's own gate criterion, listed() - unplaced(), not by hand-picking. The appearance was false. mlir_to_cpp stands its chunker down for a body that accumulates across the width by searching emitted text for a needle, and the needle was `tile_matmul` while the matmul arm writes TILE_DEGENERATE_MATMUL -- 0 corpus artefacts contain the former, 5 the latter. So a matmul was chunked on its flat element count while the arm went on indexing the unchunked extents, and the UB check passed because it sized the chunk. The emitter had stopped DETECTING what it still committed, and the 12928 sibling faulted 507035 at aclrtSynchronizeStream on an Ascend910B2. With the needle matching, both rows refuse again on the bound they always had. The lesson for this file: a backlog entry disappearing because a tool stopped complaining is not the same as the work being finished, and the gate cannot tell the two apart -- it reads which files exist. The 12928 sibling is still not in this file, because its .pto places it. 2026-11-09: and it leaves AGAIN, this time because the PTO path places it rather than because a tool stopped complaining -- the distinction this paragraph exists to draw. Its PTO refusal read 'N=16160 must be a multiple of Nb=64', which is true of Nb=64 and is not a property of the shape: 16160 = 32 x 505, Nb=32 divides N and is a legal multiple of the 16 cube fractal, and the L0B footprint only SHRINKS (16 KB against l0_b_size=65536). pick_nb_for_dtype now halves to find a divisor as pick_kb already did. The artefact is stored and ptoas 0.68 --pto-arch=a2 accepts it at rc=0, so this is the same criterion that already keeps the 12928 sibling out. Its AscendC column still refuses on the UB bound it always had, and nothing here claims otherwise.

left_the_backlog_2026_11_08: glm_5_3/argmax_glm53_1x154880 and kimi_k3/argmax_k3_1x163840. The AscendC path places both now, through the CHUNKED ARGMAX arm -- an argmax carries a (max, index) pair whose index means nothing without its chunk base, so the partials reduce pairwise on the scalar unit rather than into a tile accumulator. Both are device-verified against ORACLE 41 at the exact index. Their PTO refusals are unchanged and still accurate, so what leaves is the claim that NEITHER emitter places them; the `needs` text each carried about generalising rspto's chunked path still describes real PTO-side work and survives on the two eight-row argmaxes, which need this rescue composed with the row-blocked one and get neither.
left_the_backlog_2026_11_08_topk: glm_5_3/router_topk_glm53_1x288_k8. The AscendC path places them now, through __tile_topk_f32 (and __tile_sigmoid_f32 for the K3 router), and all are device-verified at the exact indices against ORACLE 42 and 43. Their PTO state is unchanged and the `needs` text each carried still describes real PTO-side work -- and more of it than it said: mlir_to_pto's own topk docstring states that its Path A composition 'parses and verifies' but does NOT claim to compute top-k, and that other shapes take 'the stub passthrough, which is a head extract and not a sort'. What leaves this file is only the claim that NEITHER emitter places them.
